newsitem.title: UK: Expectations of broad EMU mostly steady - JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Expectations of broad EMU mostly steady - JP Morgan.

text.p: Market expectations of a broad-based start to European economic and monetary union (EMU) were little changed this week, prices monitored by JP Morgan showed on Friday.

JP Morgan's "EMU" calculator showed optimism about starting EMU was steady to a touch softer in most monitored countries, though Ireland and the United Kingdom bucked the trend with market expectations for both rising slightly.
For Ireland, the assumed probability of a 1999 EMU start rose to 57 percentage points from 48 percent in the past week and the UK's chances were up to 38 percent from 36 percent.
The so-called "Club Med" countries saw their chances mostly lower in the week, save for Italy which saw its chances steady at 67 percent.
The assumed probability by the market that Spain and Portugal will join in 1999 decreased slightly to 80 percentage points from 82 percent last week, respectively.
Denmark, however, saw the biggest slide with probabilities slipping to 39 percentage points in the week from 42 percent last week.
The U.S. investment firm's calculator -- which is derived from the interest rate swaps market -- showed the readings for France and Belgium remained at 100 percent.
JP Morgan points out there is a reasonable margin of error in overall probability levels of between three and five points.
The probabilities are derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor, and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
